articleTitle: Temperature and Gas Concentration Imaging of LAS Tomography from Gaussian Filtered SART with Artifact Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Laser absorption spectroscopy (LAS) is widely applied for tomographic imaging of temperature and gas concentration in combustion fields. To improve the imaging accuracy and reduce artifacts, the Gaussian filter is added in the iteration of simultaneous algebraic reconstruction technique (SART) as a smoothing operator, and an artifact removal method is developed based on the correlation between flame temperature and concentration. Symmetrical and asymmetrical distributions of temperature and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> mole fraction obtained from the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation were reconstructed in the numerical verification. The proposed Gaussian filtered SART with artifact removal performed well with the fewest artifacts and lowest reconstruction errors compared to typical SART-based methods. The exit of a high-temperature wind tunnel was measured for experiment verification, and temperatures at the center of the wind tunnel exit in 11 different cases were measured by the thermocouple as a reference. Temperature and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}_{2}\mathbf{O}$</tex> mole fraction distributions reconstructed by the proposed method were smooth, and its variation trend was consistent with the real condition. The maximum relative error of temperature of the proposed method was only 5.29%, much smaller than that of the typical SART with a median filter. Both numerical and experiment verifications demonstrated the ability of the proposed method in high-accuracy tomographic imaging.

articleTitle: Detection of Dental Caries Based on GV Black Classification Utilizing Yolov8 from X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Tooth decay, a prevalent ailment, often eludes detection through conventional visual and tactile examination, especially in its early stages. This study presents a new approach utilizing Yolov8-based multiclass classification on X-ray images to identify dental caries according to the GV Black classification. The classification has seven categories: classes from I-VI, and the normal dental structure. The study implemented the Y olov8 model on the datasets and assessed its accuracy, precision, and recall for detecting dental caries. The performance metrics evaluation shows good result for the You Only Look Once (Yolov8), a real-time object detection model. The model displays a recall of 84.9%, mAP50 of 91.5%, mAP50-95 of 73.6%, precision of 96.3%, and mAP50 of 91.5% without data augmentation such as flip, rotation, and shear. The scores improved to 96.6% precision, 92.1% recall, 95.1% mAP50, and 75.9% mAP50-95 after data augmentation. These results highlight the efficacy of the Yolov8 model for detecting dental caries based on GV Black Classification, while at the same time indicating further scopes of refinement. The performance according to the values presented can be compared to existing models as it also surpassed the average benchmarks. It is one of the most promising applications of artificial intelligence and deep learning in the medical field, especially in dental diseases detection.

articleTitle: Discrimination of Different Nanoparticles Based on Narrowband Magnetic Particle Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) is a new imaging modality that allows to visualize the spatial distribution of magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) based on the measurement of their nonlinear dynamic magnetization. In MPI, the unique spectral signatures of different particles induced in an ac magnetic field allow to distinguish the types of MNPs via color-MPI techniques, which is of great importance to disease diagnosis and treatment. Successful signal separation has been reported with broadband MPI approach. In this paper, a new method of dual-color MPI based on single-harmonic-based narrowband MPI approach is proposed to quantitatively visualize the spatial distribution of two different MNPs. The imaging principle of narrow-band MPI is introduced while the mathematical expression of dual-color MPI is derived. Simulations are performed to evaluate the performance of the proposed method for the discrimination of the different MNPs. Only the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonics are used for image reconstruction in the narrowband MPI. A row-based iterative reconstruction is adopted in the simulations. Different parameters in the algorithm are tested and the reconstruction images are compared for parameter selection. Simulation results confirm the feasibility of the proposed approach for effective discrimination of two different MNPs. The cross-talk between different channels is analyzed and discussed in the last section.

articleTitle: Waveformer: Innovative Token Mixing for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Recent advancements in Transformer-based methods have demonstrated remarkable performance in various low-level vision tasks, including image denoising, image deblurring, and image demosaicing. However, many of these methods face limitations in plug-and-play image restoration due to two key drawbacks: inefficiencies in the Self-Attention mechanism of Transformers and the inability to dynamically adjust normalized features using spatial information from the input image. To address these issues, we propose a novel attention mechanism called Wave-Attention and use it as a token mixing strategy to build Waveformer, an asymmetric U-Net model. In the encoder, Wave-Attention aggregates tokens in wave representation, efficiently capturing dependencies based on learned amplitude and phase. Additionally, our decoder utilizes a revised spatial adaptive normalization (Spade) module to enhance normalized features using the spatial context of the input noisy image. The proposed encoder-decoder architecture underpins an effective deep learning-based denoiser. In our experiments, we first train Waveformer using noise level maps and noisy images as inputs for image denoising, enabling the model to handle a wide range of noise levels. We then integrate the well-trained model into the half quadratic splitting algorithm as a denoiser to tackle image deblurring and image demosaicing tasks. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses the latest learning-based methods in various image restoration tasks.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Mushroom Classification: Differentiating Edible and Poisonous Species Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Damage caused by mushroom poisoning has significantly risen over the years. It is hard to determine the difference between edible and poisonous ones, for they have similar physical features. However, this study has introduced a system using image processing algorithms utilizing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract important characteristics from mushrooms to identify edible and poisonous varieties. Samples were tested wherein images of mushrooms were aided with Python, specifically Jupyter and Spyder Notebook, to create different Deep Learning Models and identify the most accurate one using various metrics such as Accuracy, AUC, Min Squared error, Precision and Recall. The developed system was able to have an accuracy rate of 99.08% indicating that the model can effectively classify the edible and poisonous mushrooms.

articleTitle: Weighted Multi-Camera Stereo Vision Based on Geometric Relationships of Feature Edges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Improving the accuracy of visual applications for measurement has always been a hot topic in the fields of aerospace, automotive manufacturing and robotics. The multi-camera system, which can provide redundant information from multiple views to improve measurement accuracy and robustness, has been widely used. Due to factors such as pixel dispersion, image noise and mismatches, the extraction accuracy of corresponding key points in images is greatly affected. Traditional 3D point reconstruction algorithms assign the same weight to the corresponding key points in each image, which lacks consideration of the different extraction accuracy of the key points, resulting in lower measurement accuracy. In this paper, weighted multi-camera stereo vision by considering geometric relationships is proposed, which can be extended to the measurement of features with theoretical geometric relationships in projection by any number of cameras. A five-camera measurement system is designed for accuracy verification. The experimental results indicate that by reasonable weight computation, the root-mean-square errors reduce 4.46%, 5.02%, 3.38% for length, width and center distance of rectangle respectively and the root-mean-square errors reduce 3.26%, 10.69%, 2.63% for length, width and center distance of oval shape respectively compared with the least square method. Besides, the measurement robustness is also proved to have a significant improvement.

articleTitle: Quantum Neural Network for Accelerated Magnetic Resonance Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Magnetic resonance image reconstruction starting from undersampled k-space data requires the recovery of many potential nonlinear features, which is very difficult for algorithms to recover these features. In recent years, the development of quantum computing has discovered that quantum convolution can improve network accuracy, possibly due to potential quantum advantages. This article proposes a hybrid neural network containing quantum and classical networks for fast magnetic resonance imaging, and conducts experiments on a quantum computer simulation system. The experimental results indicate that the hybrid network has achieved excellent reconstruction results, and also confirm the feasibility of applying hybrid quantum-classical neural networks into the image reconstruction of rapid magnetic resonance imaging.

articleTitle: YOLO-Based Defect Detection for Metal Sheets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a YOLO-based deep learning (DL) model for automatic defect detection to solve time-consuming and labor-intensive in industrial manufacturing. In our experiments, the images of metal sheets are used as the dataset for training the YOLO model to detect the defects on surfaces and in holes of metal sheets. However, the lack of metal sheet images significantly degrades the performance of detection accuracy. To address this issue, the ConSinGAN is used to generate a considerable amount of data. Four versions of the YOLO model (i.e., YOLOv3, v4, v7, and v9) are combined with the ConSinGAN for data augmentation. The proposed YOLOv9 model with ConSinGAN outperforms the other YOLO models with an accuracy of 91.3%, and a detection time of 146 ms. The proposed YOLOv9 model is integrated into manufacturing hardware and a supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) to establish a practical automated optical inspection (AOI) system. Additionally, the proposed automated defect detection is easily applied to other components in industrial manufacturing.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer Based Automated Model for Enhancing Lung Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer related mortality. The early detection and classification of the cancers tissues will reduce the mortalities rate. The present research focus on the development of automated classification model for lung and colon cancers tissues based on the histopathology images. The present work encompasses a vision transformer (ViT) based model to enhance diagnostic accuracy of lung cancers tissues. The proposed model utilizes the self-attention mechanism of ViT to focus on essential features present in histopathologicals images. The proposed model has been validated using two different dataset namely LC25000 & IQ-OTH/NCCD with 25000 & 1096 images respectively. The performance of proposed model is compared with traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) model and it has been observed the based model outforms better in terms of accuracy which - 98.80% & 99.09% respectively for datasets.

articleTitle: Median Based Annoying Spikes Adaptive Denoising (ASAD)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: An approach based on median concept to detect and trim annoying impulses of the form of salt and pepper noise is proposed. The proposed Annoying Spikes Adaptive Denoising (ASAD) approach works in the spatial domain and can be applied to a 2D signals through a sliding window. A window size of 4x4 was found sufficient to reveal the local standard deviation of the corrupting noise. The Median of the window is subtracted from the window samples, the resulting absolute values are then compared to the local standard deviation. If a sample within the window is found higher in magnitude than the local standard deviation, that sample will take the value of the median of the window, otherwise, it will retain its value. A scaling parameter is introduced to control the value of the revealed local standard deviation and hence controlling the amount of trimming of the lengths of spikes. When compared to benchmark schemes in the area, such as Hybrid median filter (HMF), Adaptive Median Filter (AMF) and Weighted Median Filter (WMF), the proposed ASAD approach has shown a leading performance in terms of resolution, CNR, SNR, and a competitive performance in terms of edge detection, PSNR, FSIM and MSSIM.

articleTitle: Enhancing Process Image Analysis with Adaptive Thresholding and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning model specifically designed to effectively classify display Mura images. The model leverages advanced deep learning techniques and computer vision methods to identify and categorize various types of Mura based on their unique digital signatures and visual patterns. It aims to provide fast and accurate classification results, enabling real-time processing of large-scale image data. The model is expected to significantly enhance content management and user experience with display Mura, and it can be innovatively applied across various fields of image classification.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Persons in Point Clouds from Photon Counting Lidar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Segmentation of persons at large distances is desired for surveillance and reconnaissance in security and defense applications. Today lidar sensors can provide high-resolution three dimensional (3D) point clouds of scenes at kilometer ranges which can be used for this task. In this work, we evaluate a method for deep learning semantic segmentation of persons in lidar point clouds for long-range surveillance and reconnaissance applications. The method is applied to point clouds from a time-correlated single-photon counting Iidar at ranges from a few hundred meters to around one kilometer in open and forested terrain, which is a new application for person detection. The network utilizes fusion of voxel-based features and point-based features. A slice-based approach is applied, where smaller parts of larger scans are processed separately, which enables near real-time segmentation. The method is trained and validated on annotated data from fifteen different outdoor scenes from three geographical areas, and evaluated on a separate outdoor scene. In experimental results, the method achieves 84.3% in terms of mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for the person and background classes on the test set. The results show that the presented approach for person segmentation in photon counting lidar data is suitable for long-range applications such as surveillance and reconnaissance.

articleTitle: Measurement of Absorption Spectroscopy Based on a Dispersion-Managed Dual-Comb Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy is a competitive means of laser absorption spectroscopy owing to broad spectral range and high spectral resolution. Single-cavity dual-comb systems based on mode-locked lasers hold promising potential for further simplifying dual-comb spectroscopy. Two combs possess natural coherence because of common mode noise suppression. Herein, we proposed an all-fiber dispersion-managed dual-comb laser to broaden the spectra of dual combs. The output laser with a 3-dB bandwidth as broad as 9 nm at 1.5 μm was experimentally obtained. Dual combs were realized by the walk-off of orthogonal polarization modes and directly employed to absorption spec-troscopy due to their overlapped spectra. In order to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of dual-comb measurement, interferogram averaging was conducted, where the signal-to-noise ratio was generally proportional to the square root of averaging times. Besides, phase and frequency jitter was corrected by cross-correlation method. High resolution absorption lines of hydrogen cyanide from P18 to P26 were measured. Positions of measured absorption lines were in line with ones in HITRAN database, with an average error of approximate 1 pm. To the best of our knowledge, the 9-line result was the broadest bandwidth of polarization-multiplexed single-cavity dual combs without additional spectral spreading operation. The results demonstrate that the compact dual-comb spectrometer can be considered a potential candidate for quantitative measurements in practical applications.

articleTitle: Image Compressed Sensing Based on Vision-Inspired Importance Maps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This paper presents a novel image compressed sensing framework that leverages human vision-inspired importance maps to guide the compression process. Unlike traditional methods that compress images without considering perceptual relevance, our approach selectively samples pixels based on their visual saliency and geometric significance. The framework begins by generating an importance map that combines visual saliency, obtained through LayerCAM, with geometric features like edge information. These maps dictate the adaptive sampling of pixels, ensuring that the most visually important information is retained. In the decoding stage, the sampled pixels are reconstructed using prior information-based models such as the Deep Image Prior and Manifold Modeling in Embedded Space. These models effectively restore the image while preserving its critical visual characteristics. To evaluate the performance of our framework, we introduce two new similarity criteria: Weighted PSNR (WPSNR) and Weighted SSIM (WSSIM), both tailored to assess the perceptual quality of images. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional image compression techniques, especially in maintaining perceptual quality at low sampling rates. This framework shows great promise for applications in areas where preserving visual fidelity is crucial, such as high-quality image compression and digital brain modeling. The integration of visual importance into the compression process represents a significant advancement in the field of image processing, offering a more efficient and perceptually aware approach to image compression.

articleTitle: MineSeeker: A Novel Design for Detecting Explosive Mines Using Low-Resolution Thermal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Landmines, particularly the PFM-1 Butterfly landmine, continue to pose a significant threat to civilian populations in conflict zones around the world. Traditional detection methods, such as manual searches, drone surveillance, and optical detection technologies, are often rendered ineffective due to the PFM-1's camouflaged coating and small size. In response to these challenges, our research introduces a novel approach utilizing an enhanced version of the YOLOv8 deep learning algorithm, integrated with cubic spline interpolation, to improve detection accuracy with low-resolution thermal imagery. Our innovative algorithmic approach enables the development of a cost-effective and compact mine detection system. This system employs affordable, low-resolution thermal cameras and is designed to operate efficiently on low-computational power devices like the Raspberry Pi. The integration of cubic spline interpolation enhances image resolution, allowing for more accurate detection of mines despite the limitations of low-resolution thermal imagery. Experimental results have demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed design, showcasing its ability to offer a scalable and efficient solution for mine detection. The enhanced YOLOv8 algorithm significantly improves detection accuracy, making the system viable for deployment in various operational environments. Additionally, the adaptability of this approach extends its potential applications beyond mine detection, suggesting its utility in other object detection scenarios. By providing a more accessible and reliable method for detecting landmines, our system holds the promise of reducing the risk to civilian populations in affected areas. The advancements presented in this research not only address the immediate need for improved mine detection but also contribute to the broader field of object detection technology, potentially influencing future developments in related areas.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a 6 DOF Arbiter Robotic Arm for Games of the General (Salpakan) Using Yolov8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This study presents the design and development of an autonomous 6 degrees of freedom (DOF) arbiter robotic arm for the Filipino board game “Game of the Generals” or “Salpakan.” The robotic arm is equipped with a parallel jaw gripper and made intelligent using deep learning models from the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family, specifically YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv10. These models enable real-time object detection and decision-making, allowing the arm to enforce game rules, determine the outcome of challenges, and retrieve losing pieces. A dataset consisting of 30 classes was created, representing the various pieces used by opposing players. The models were trained using a batch size of32 and 100 epochs. The performance of the YOLO models was evaluated using confusion matrices, with results showing that YOLOv8 achieved the highest accuracy, making it the most suitable model for this application. YOLOv8 produced the highest mean average precision (mAP) scores, with mAP50 and mAP50-95 values of 99.5% and 85.4%, respectively. This integration of AI and robotics enhances the fairness and functionality of strategic board games, providing an automated and impartial arbiter for the “Game of the Generals.” This research demonstrates the potential of combining deep learning and robotics to innovate traditional board games, ensuring accuracy and efficiency in game management.

articleTitle: Space Target Pose Estimation Based on High-Level Geometric Correspondences for Single-Photon LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Single-photon LiDAR is considered to be one of the most promising techniques for space target pose estimation due to its low power consumption, small size, and lightweight. And it is widely used in space target rendezvous, docking, and landing. However, such processing needs to address plenty of high-noise photon point clouds with limited resources and be completed in a very short time. To address these challenges, a global optimization method of pose estimation based on high-level geometric correspondences is proposed in this work. First, a K-Nearest Neighbors undirected graph is designed for describing the geometrical consistency of correspondences and a degree matrix is calculated to remove the false correspondences. In addition, a robust error metric based on Cauchy's function is introduced, which can effectively speed up the convergence of the optimization and iteratively update the parameters of the transformation matrix. The process of scanning a satellite with the single-photon LiDAR to obtain photon point clouds was simulated using the Monte Carlo method. Simulation results show that the proposed method can accurately estimate the pose of the satellite with a noise rate of 5%, 10%, and 15% in a time less than 1 second, revealing that it is of an obvious advantage in both efficiency and robustness when dealing with large-scale and noisy photon point clouds.

articleTitle: Human Blood Type Classification Using Feature Selection and Optimized Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Blood type classification, a fundamental aspect of medical diagnosis is traditionally and manually administered by registered skilled medical technologists. In this study, the proponent developed an intelligent model for human blood typing using image processing, feature extraction, and advanced machine learning methodologies. The dataset underwent a process from image acquisition, image processing, segmentation, binary conversion, and feature extraction. Univariate feature selection and the chi2 algorithm were employed to refine the original thirty-nine features down to the top twenty features. Seven machine learning algorithms were explored using default parameters. The models were then optimized using GridSearch to further enhance their performances. In LR, Blood types O+, A-, and B+ displayed the lowest F1 scores, yielding a macro-average of 89%. Meanwhile, KNN showed its lowest F1 score of 77% for Blood type B+, contributing to a macro-average of 91%. Similarly, SVM manifested the lowest F1 score for Blood type B+, resulting in a macro-average of 90%. Increasing the size of the training set size and validation set size should be taken into consideration in order to further enhance model performance. This study contributes insights into developing and optimizing intelligent models for blood typing and potential avenues for future research and model enhancements by integrating cutting-edge technologies.

articleTitle: Eddy-Current Suppression with Self-Compensation Technique in Ultra-Low-Field MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The ultralow field magnetic resonance imaging (ULF MRI) system operates in a static magnetic field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_0<250 \mu\boldsymbol{\mathrm{T}}$</tex>. As superconducting magnets are no longer required, ULF MRI offers advantages such as improved portability, significantly lower cost, and insensitivity to metallic objects. However, the ULF MRI system faces the challenge of poor signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The highly sensitive superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs) can detect the weak ULF MRI signal to enhance the SNR. A pre-polarization field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{B}_{\boldsymbol{p}})$</tex> in the order of tens of mT is used to pre-polarize the sample at the beginning of MRI sequences. However, the rapid switch-off of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_{\boldsymbol{p}}$</tex> current induces eddy currents in the conductively shielded room (CSR) and the surrounding conductors, increasing the MRI system's dead time before signal acquisition. In this case, the gain of the SQUID readout electronics must be decreased by reducing its feedback resistance, which will worsen the detector sensitivity and lower the SNR. Herein, we describe a self-compensation technique through a programmable hardware system with a digital-to-analog converter. The compensation parameters are set based on the complex transient residual field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_{\mathbf{t}\mathbf{r}}$</tex> caused by eddy currents. With this technique, the transient voltage outputs Vtr of the SQUID electronics caused by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{B}_{\mathbf{t}\mathbf{r}}$</tex> are well suppressed so that larger feedback resistance becomes feasible, and the SNR of the ULF-MRI image is improved. The experimental results reveal that this technique would reduce the maximal output range of eddy current by approximately 79.2% and improve the SNR of ULF MRI images by a factor of 2. We employed a convolutional neural network U-net to reduce noise and improve SNR further. With its potential to significantly enhance SNR in ULF MRI, this compensation technique will be of great importance in human imaging, marking a significant advancement in the field.

articleTitle: Unpaired Synthesis of IC Scanning Electron Microscopy Images with Structural Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The analysis of Integrated Circuit (IC) Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) images plays a crucial role in the reliability and authenticity investigation of modern ICs. It pertains to the task of predicting masks, which indicate the pixel-level position of different circuit elements, from IC SEM images, and it is now usually achieved through deep learning models that need to be trained or finetuned over a considerably large labeled dataset of IC SEM images. Furthermore, such labeled dataset is usually not publicly available and is costly to obtain. Recently, unpaired synthesis of IC SEM images, which aims to translate masks indicating IC circuit elements into IC SEM images with corresponding circuit elements, has made it possible for semi-supervised learning models to perform comparably well in IC image analysis but with lower dependency on labeled data. However, existing methods for unpaired synthesis of IC SEM images suffer from the low consistency of circuit element patterns between masks and synthetic images. In this paper, we propose a Structural Constrained Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Network (SC-CycleGAN), that leverages on CycleGAN and novel structural constraints to synthesize IC SEM images with improved consistency of circuit element patterns. Experiments on real masks and IC SEM images have demonstrated the superior performance of our proposed SC-CycleGAN.

articleTitle: High Accuracy Vision-Laser Post-Welding Defect Detection and Segmentation Method Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Recently, the advent of deep learning technology has led to the exploration and application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) based welding defect detection methods by numerous researchers in several industrial settings. However, most CNN-based methods are single-task networks that can only classify the type of welding defect, lacking the capacity to provide additional information such as the shape of the defect. This limitation hinders their application in more diverse scenarios. This paper proposes a high-accuracy, CNN-based method for post-welding defect detection and segmentation using the Vision-laser system. The proposed method, which comprises a multitask CNN, can simultaneously detect, classify, and segment the area of the welding defect. This approach allows for the acquisition of more comprehensive information about the welding defect compared to existing single-task methods. A Vision-laser system is assembled and calibrated for data collection and testing. The proposed network is trained and evaluated on this dataset. The results demonstrate that the method achieved a mean accuracy of 99.58%, a mean precision of 99.43%, and a recall of 97.05% on the welding defect detection task. Additionally, it achieved a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 92.58% on the welding defect segmentation task. The proposed method exhibits high accuracy in both defect detection and segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Enhanced Spike-Event Neuromorphic Detection of Quasi-DC Signals in Noisy Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: A technique aimed to work with weak and extremely noisy signals, is presented. The preliminary results of this study indicate that DC or quasi-DC low-intensity light illumination of targets at the presence of strong background noise leads to enhanced Dynamic Vision Detection (DVS) detection, at reduced time resolution. Overall, our technique is aimed at harnessing noise rather eliminating or mitigating it. Exploiting this technique could allow neuromorphic circuits to work with weak and extremely noisy signals, and to develop new detection concepts and applications. The impact of the stochastic resonance on the DC enhanced detection process at the presence of strong amount of noise, is being investigated.

Author Keywords: enhanced detection of weak DC or quasi DC light intensities in strong background noise

articleTitle: Vision-Based Waste Classification for Handheld PET Bottles and Paper Using Convolutional Neural Network and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Most object classification models use steady images in a fully controlled environment as a dataset to get the highest possible accuracy. Existing classification systems aligned with waste materials also have generalized outputs ie. biodegradable or nonbiodegradable. This study aims to integrate images dataset of handheld PET bottles and paper wastes on deep learning methods CNN, YOLOv5, and ResNet50. Mentioned transfer learning techniques are evaluated and compared to conclude which of them produce the highest classification accuracy. The tests conducted resulted in a similar result of 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> classification accuracy for all 3 models in consideration of the 2,400 image datasets equally divided between the two proponent materials, wherein 1,980 are designated as training data, while 400 are testing data.

articleTitle: An Interdisciplinary Framework for Systematic Innovation: A Case Study on Nature-Inspired Imaging Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This research presents a novel interdisciplinary framework designed to uncover connections across diverse knowledge domains through advanced semantic modeling techniques. A case study focused on nature-inspired imaging solutions illustrates the potential of the framework. Innovation often emerges at the intersection of various scientific fields. However, manually identifying these intersections within the vast scientific literature is impractical. By exploring how biological principles can inspire the development of advanced imaging technologies, such as image sensors for rapid motion tracking, we underscore the critical role of interdisciplinary research in the promotion of technological innovation. Our framework systematically identifies and analyzes cross-domain connections, showcasing the potential of automated bioinspired approaches to drive innovation from the early stages. This research highlights how semantic modeling can bridge gaps between disparate fields, facilitating the discovery of novel insights, and fostering a more integrated approach to academic research. By automating the process of identifying relevant intersections within extensive literature, our framework not only enhances research efficiency, but also broadens the scope for innovative solutions. Ultimately, this work underscores the value of interdisciplinary collaboration and the transformative potential of bioinspired methodologies in the advancement of technology. The findings presented offer an actionable roadmap for leveraging semantic modeling to accelerate the pace of innovation in various domains.

articleTitle: Multimodal Machine Learning for Multifactor Geospatial Prioritization of Suitable Healthcare Facility Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This study introduces a comprehensive multifactor geospatial methodology to identify and prioritize optimal locations for the construction of new healthcare facilities. Building on a previously developed geospatial machine learning pipeline designed to predict suitable sites, we introduce two complementary machine learning-based methodologies to enhance the decision-making process. The first methodology employs a population-density-based approach with the objective of maximizing the impact of new healthcare facilities by prioritizing areas with the highest population densities. This strategy ensures that the greatest number of individuals can benefit from new healthcare services. The second methodology is a geographical-distribution-based approach, which focuses on promoting equitable access to healthcare by targeting underserved and underrepresented areas, regardless of administrative boundaries. By prioritizing locations that currently lack sufficient healthcare resources, this approach aims to reduce disparities in healthcare accessibility and improve overall equity in resource allocation. The integration of these two methodologies provides a balanced framework that addresses both the need for widespread impact and the imperative for equitable access. The results of this study are expected to help improve healthcare access, ensuring that new facilities are strategically placed to serve densely populated regions and underserved communities, ultimately leading to more equitable and effective healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Optimized Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting Using Ziv-Zakai Bound
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting (MRF) has emerged as a promising quantitative imaging technique within the field of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), offers comprehensive insights into tissue properties by simultaneously acquiring multiple tissue parameter maps in a single acquisition. Sequence optimization is crucial for improving the accuracy and efficiency of MRF. In this work, a novel framework for MRF sequence optimization is proposed based on the Ziv-Zakai bound (ZZB). Unlike the Cramér-Rae bound (CRB), which aims to enhance the quality of a single fingerprint signal with deterministic parameters, ZZB provides insights into evaluating the minimum mismatch probability for pairs of fingerprint signals within the specified parameter range in MRF. Specifically, the explicit ZZB is derived to establish a lower bound for the discrimination error in the fingerprint signal matching process within MRF. This bound illuminates the intrinsic limitations of MRF sequences, thereby fostering a deeper understanding of existing sequence performance. Subsequently, an optimal experiment design problem based on ZZB was formulated to ascertain the optimal scheme of acquisition parameters, maximizing discrimination power of MRF between different tissue types. Preliminary numerical experiments show that the optimized ZZB scheme outperforms both the conventional and CRB schemes in terms of the reconstruction accuracy of multiple parameter maps.

articleTitle: Growth Stage Classification on Lettuce Cultivars Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This study explores the application of deep learning models for classifying the growth stages of lettuce cultivars. The main focus of this study is on comparing the performance of the YOLOv10 and DETR algorithms in identifying four distinct growth stages: early, head formation, leafy, and harvesting. By taking advantage of computer vision techniques and a dataset of 173 images, the study aims to compare transformer-based and anchor-based algorithms in determining which one is better. Results indicate that YOLOv10 outperforms DETR, achieving higher precision (87.9% vs. 64.3%), recall (76.9% vs. 48.3%), and F1 score (0.818 vs. 0.552). The findings suggest that anchor-based approach of YOLOv10 is more efficient on growth stage classification of lettuce, likely due to its ability to handle small object detection and its optimized computational efficiency. By enhancing the accuracy of growth stage classification, the study contributes to sustainable agricultural practices, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal 12, which promotes sustainable consumption and production patterns.

articleTitle: 2-D Interpolated Discrete Fourier Transform for High-Accuracy In-Plane Displacement and Rotation Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This article introduces a novel two-dimensional interpolated discrete Fourier transform (2-D IpDFT) algorithm, specifically developed to achieve high-accuracy in-plane displacement and rotation measurements in machine vision applications. The 2-D IpDFT algorithm addresses the limitations of current methods by providing enhanced precision in estimating both frequency and phase, which are crucial for accurate pose estimation. The underlying principles of the algorithm are thoroughly detailed. To evaluate the effectiveness of the 2-D IpDFT, comprehensive simulations were conducted, analyzing the impact of varying pattern pitches and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels on measurement accuracy. Beyond simulations, the algorithm's practical applicability was validated through experiments using a high-precision nanopositioning stage. The experimental results were compelling, revealing that the 2-D IpDFT algorithm achieved root mean square errors (RMSEs) as low as 10.7 nm and 13.6 nm for x and y displacements, respectively, and 2.1 μrad for z-axis rotation. Notably, these precise measurements were obtained even with a relatively low-resolution camera of 640x480 pixels. These findings underscore the significant potential of the 2-D IpDFT algorithm for high-precision pose estimation in various machine vision systems, including automated manufacturing, quality control, and robotics. By offering substantial improvements in both precision and reliability over existing techniques, this study positions the 2-D IpDFT algorithm as a promising tool for advancing the capabilities of vision-based measurement technologies.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Sensitivity of Capacitive Tactile Sensors with Different Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: It is important to adjust the gripping force based on tactile data for ensuring successful and safe gripping in a robot's grasping process. This research aims to evaluate the performance of capacitive tactile sensors developed by Beijing Tashan Technology Co. Ltd., which have potential to be used for robot-assisted electrical capacitance tomography (ECT). There are two types of sensor structures: TS-E-1 with a multi-sensing correlation array and TS-E-2 with a multi-sensing independent array. These sensors are designed for use in robotic grippers and hands and capable for measuring three-dimensional (3D) force. The analysis in this work is focused on how the sensors perform when they come into contact with different materials, including metal, cotton, plastic, aluminium, rubber and clay. The experiment aims to identify the self-capacitance of 3D force. The percentage change in capacitance in response to the applied normal force is measured and analysed to figure out the sensitivity of each sensor with different materials and force ranges. From the experimental results, it can be seen that the sensitivity of the two sensors changes dramatically with different materials and in different measurement range, from 8.97%/N to 108.31%/N. The obtained data would help application of the sensors in robot grippers to handle various objects of different materials.

articleTitle: High-Performance Face Identification Using Randomly Selected Channels from Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: With the recent development of information technology, the importance of protecting personal information has increased. Because of the vulnerability in passwords, biometric authentication is now being used as a method of personal information protection. However, biometric authentication has the possibility of malicious authentication due to the emergence of technology that can generate biometric data that is difficult to duplicate. Therefore, this study aimed to solve the security problems posed by Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in biometric authentication by using Hyperspectral Images (HSI). We searched for solutions to the problems identified in previous studies, such as the inability to correctly identify individuals who have not been previously learned and the length of time required for identification. In this paper, we used three channels of data randomly selected from hyperspectral face images for learning to identify individuals by binary classification into “learned subject (class)” and “unlearned subjects (classes)”. In this case, discriminators based on the least-squares generative adversarial network (LSGAN) model was developed for each class using three randomly selected channels of data from the HSI for two class classification. The proposed method significantly reduced the identification time and achieved very high discrimination accuracy in all classes. In addition, the results showed high accuracy throughout multiple face identification experiments.

articleTitle: End-to-End Through-Wall Human Localization Network Using Raw Radar ADC Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The radar signal processing algorithm is one of the core processes in through-wall radar human localization technology. However, traditional algorithms often struggle to adaptively handle low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) echo signals in challenging and dynamic through-wall application environments. These environments, characterized by complex and varying conditions such as multi-path reflections and signal attenuation through different wall materials, exacerbate the difficulties in accurately localizing human targets. In this paper, we introduce a novel end-to-end through-wall radar human localization network, which directly processes raw radar Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) signals without any preprocessing. By bypassing traditional signal processing stages, our approach leverages the raw data to capture more comprehensive information from the environment, allowing for more robust and adaptable localization. To achieve this, we replace the conventional radar signal processing flow with the proposed DFT-based adaptive feature extraction (DAFE) module. This module employs learnable parameterized 3D complex convolution layers, which are specifically designed to extract superior feature representations from ADC signals. The ability to learn implicit features from raw data enables our network to overcome the limitations of traditional preprocessing methods, which often fail to adequately capture the nuances of low-SNR conditions. We rigorously trained and validated our proposed method on extensive data collected in real-world through-wall scenarios. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness and superiority of our approach, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve human localization accuracy in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Design of Saddle-Shaped Coils for Field Free Point Scanning in Magnetic Particle Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is an emerging medical imaging modality for quantitatively visualizing the spatial distribution of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs). In MPI, the design of the scanning coil is a critical component. It enables the rapid movement of the field free point (FFP) through the field of view (FOV) for fast imaging. Both Helmholtz coils and saddle-shaped coils are capable of generating a uniform scanning magnetic field. However, the saddle-shaped coil design is preferred due to its greater compactness. In this paper, we introduce an enhanced saddle-shaped coil design to optimize performance parameters, such as the homogeneity and efficiency of coil, through finite element method (FEM) and experiments. In addition, we also provide the geometric parameters for finite element simulation modeling of saddle-shaped coils, along with the criteria for selecting these geometric parameters. The simulation results show the influence of the geometric parameters of the saddle-shaped coil on its performance. Based on FEM and the geometric parameter analysis, we develop an improved scanning coil. The measurement results show that the saddle-shaped coil allows good homogeneity of 98.2%. In addition, 1D phantom imaging experiments are performed, which indicates a spatial resolution of 1.5 mm along the y-axis in the narrowband MPI scanner.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of YOLOv8, YOLOv9 and YOLOv10 Models in Detecting Fusarium Wilt Disease in Banana Leaf Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Agriculture is a critical component of the socio-economic landscape in the Philippines, with banana plantations playing a significant role. However, diseases such as Fusarium Wilt pose a major threat, causing substantial economic losses. Computer vision, particularly deep learning models like the You Only Look Once (YOLO) series, offers promising solutions for early disease detection. In this study, the researchers evaluate the performance of the YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv10 models in detecting Fusarium Wilt disease in banana leaf plants. The models were trained and tested using a dataset of 450 images, including 331 infected and 152 healthy leaves. The YOLO models were then evaluated on metrics including precision, recall, and mean average precision (mAP0.5-0.95). Hyperparameters were fine-tuned with batch sizes of 16, 32, and 64, and learning rates of 0.01, 0.001, and 0.0001. YOLOv8 and YOLOv9 showed inconsistent performance with varying batch sizes and learning rates, while YOLOv10 exhibited more predictable improvements, favoring lower batch sizes. Lower learning rates generally enhanced mAP50-95, though precision and recall varied. YOLOv8 and YOLOv9 achieved peak mAP50-95 with a batch size of 32 and a learning rate of 0.001, while YOLOv10 performed best with a batch size of 16 and a learning rate of 0.01. Among the models, YOLOv9 with a batch size of 32 and a learning rate of 0.001 achieved the highest mAP50-95, indicating high precision and recall in detecting Fusarium Wilt. These findings emphasize the need for systematic hyperparameter tuning to optimize YOLO models for specific tasks and resources.

articleTitle: Integrating Datasets for Driving Intention Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Vehicle driving intention recognition is an important component of autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance system (ADAS). By predicting the driving intention of the target vehicle, more information can be provided to human driver or autonomous driving system. Existing vehicle driving intention methods often only consider the lateral driving intentions of vehicles, but recognizing longitudinal driving intentions is also crucial for driving safety. This paper considers the influence of surrounding vehicles on the driving intention of the target vehicle from a microscopic perspective and proposes a model based on self-attention and cross-attention that can simultaneously predict the lateral and longitudinal driving intentions of vehicles. The NGSIM (Next Generation Simulation) dataset and HighD (Highway Drone) dataset are commonly used datasets for vehicle driving intention recognition task, but they both suffer from a significant difference in data quantity for different driving intentions. Therefore, this paper proposes a method to integrate the NGSIM and HighD datasets to balance the number of data for each class of intention. By training our model on this integrated dataset, the model's performance metrics (precision, recall, F1 score) improve by around 4% compared to the baseline model when predicting 0.5s in advance.

articleTitle: Named Entity Recognition for Safety Risks in Electrical Work
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The texts of safety risks in eletrical work describe the safety risks involved and management measures. The text records information on potential risks, risk levels, and preventive measures within the electrical work, which is crucial for extracting and mining safety risks. Named Entity Recognition for Safety Risks in Electrical Work (EWSR-NER) is a key technique for information extraction and knowledge discovery. It identifies objects related to safety risks in electrical work, such as risk level, risk factors, risk categories and protective measures, which convey critical meanings within the text. Current Named Entity Recognition (NER) is used to identify generic entities. However, their accuracy is limited by inherent linguistic irregularities in natural language texts, such as nested entities, lengthy entities, and the scarcity of domain-specific annotated corpora. To address this issue, the established standards and principles of safety risk texts in electrical work were followed to analyze the structure and characteristics of the text, developing a dataset of safety risk in electrical work. A new model, RoBERTa-BiLSTM-Efficient GlobalPointer (RoBEGP), was proposed in this paper. It uses the Robertly Optimized Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Transformers Pretraining Approach(RoBERTa) pretraining model to learn the characteristics of electrical work content and generate representation vectors. These representation vectors are input into a dynamic fusion layer, which adjusts the weights of each layer's representation vectors based on the specific requirements of the task, reducing the dimensionality from 1024 to 512. The fused vectors are input into a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory(BiLSTM) network to generate feature representations. Efficient GlobalPointer decodes these representations to identify nested entities within the text. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves an F1 score of 92.38% on a self-constructed dataset of safety risk in electrical work, identifying 11 types of entities, totaling 2408 entity nodes.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Spatial Subsampling Methods for 3D Image Projection for 2D Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: In this paper we purpose several methods for creating 2D projection image from a 3D scan such as from CT or MR scans, and then look at different types of 2.5D projections with a growing window sizes and see its effects on the efficacy of the machine learning model when combined with the selection algorithms. As such we are using Shi-Tomasi Detectors, Sobel Edge Detectors, Sum of Pixel Intensity, Center Select, and Random Selection as selection algorithms from which we select the most interesting index for a given scan, from which depending on the window size, we stack the neighboring slices in the axial plane to the channel dimension creating a 2.5D image from which we could pass into our ResNet-9 model configured for classification and train the model for a given number of epochs, under the same conditions for all of our tests, this ensures that for all of our experiments the main effector is window size and the selection algorithm. From our tests we found that the Center Select on average outperforming the other selection algorithm, this result indicate that medical information is mostly centered around the scan, and when combined with the saving of 60% less parameters, the purposed method shows a new way of processing 3D Scans for processing with a 2D CNN model.

articleTitle: Automated Industrial Load Station Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The manufacturing sector heavily relies on fast and accurate material inspection to improve product quality and productivity. Computer vision approaches based on deep learning provide superior performance for automatic material inspection over traditional methods. However, collecting a large amount of data to train a deep learning model is a challenging and expensive task, especially in an industrial environment. To address this challenge, we propose a synthetic augmentation approach, in which source data is prepared with a hybrid technique, combining synthetic data and real data to train a deep learning model, with performance evaluated on the target data. The applied approach consists of three key steps and performance evaluation indicates the ability to learn the domainvariant features and enhance the model's generalisation ability. For inspection purposes, two well-known models, YOLOv5 and YOLOv8, were employed utilizing the optimizers SGD and AdamW, respectively, which provided significant test accuracy. Building on the results, the applied approach may be recommended for similar inspection use cases in smart industry applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Field Distributions Generation for Complex Objects Using a Deep Learning-Based Image Processing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Accurately and rapidly determining the field distribution for complex objects is crucial, especially in the energy sector. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) methods have been employed to simulate thermal field flows by numerically solving the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. This methodology requires the implementation of complex procedures, such as the establishment of the computational domain, the discretization of the partial differential equation, and so forth. Consequently, it is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. This paper presents a novel approach for predicting thermal field distributions using a deep learning-based image processing method. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which are known for their ability to generate complex images, present a new opportunity for simulating thermal field distributions. In contrast to conventional CFD techniques, GANs are capable of directly generating thermal field distribution images from input object images without the necessity of solving NS equations, thereby significantly simplifying the process. The approach is based on the StarGAN v2 architecture, which has been shown to be efficient for generating complex images. The method is applied to a dataset constructed using traditional CFD methods, and the results demonstrate that the generated thermal field images closely match the original images, with a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) value exceeding 0.92, this confirms the effectiveness and precision of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Grayscale Images Flame Detections Based on Colorazion Algorithm and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Flame detection algorithms are crucial for real-time fire monitoring using surveillance cameras. Current flame detection algorithms perform excellently on color cameras; however, many night vision cameras can only capture grayscale images, making flame detection less effective in such scenarios. Traditional flame detection algorithms rely heavily on color features, especially the red and yellow hues of flames. Conversely, grayscale images lack color information, making these algorithms ineffective. To address this limitation, we propose a novel flame detection algorithm that integrates the DeOldify model with the you only look once(YOLOv8) model. DeOldify can effectively add color to grayscale images. YOLOv8 is a powerful object detection model that excels in identifying various objects within an image. This algorithm leverages DeOldify's colorization capabilities and YOLOv8's powerful object detection abilities to enhance flame detection accuracy in grayscale images. This algorithm has been tested multiple times on public datasets, converting original images to grayscale and then colorizing them to construct the dataset. The results show that, compared to grayscale images, this algorithm improves the mean average precision (mAP@0.5) by 19.7% on different validation sets, by 4% on different training sets, and by 12.9% on grayscale images captured by night vision cameras. By comparing the training results of models such as YOLOv8n and YOLOv8s, the colorized images improve the model's performance. This demonstrates the high generalizability of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Sentinel-2 Satellite Image for Rice Growth Phase Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Sentinel-2 satellite image is one of the big data for remote sensing. This research explores the usage of U-Net model for segmentation of rice fields and CNN Model for classification of rice growth phase on SentineL-2 L2A satellite image. This study investigates the use of the U-net method for segmentation. Rice growth phases are classified using CNN model. The results show that CNN model can work better for various computer vision tasks, including preprocessing of existing satellite data for rice growth phases. For the suggested semantic segmentation model, the accuracy and IoU score values for the proposed semantic segmentation model were 0.99 and 0.66, respectively. Conversely, the suggested CNN classification model for rice growth phase, the accuracy was 0.86, while specificity was 0.97 and sensitivity was 0.85. The goal of this research is to establish the viability of such a system and to pave the way for future research including rice field extraction and rice growth phase classification using satellite imagery. The segmentation and classification model has shown excellent performance. However, the model still struggles to accurately identify the correct pixels belonging to a specific mask for segmentation or correctly recognize the right class for a specific group of area based on the spectral indices, as evidenced by a few samples in the results.

articleTitle: PDAST: Paradigm Towards Weather Domain Adaptation for 3D Detection Based on Density Aware Pooling and Self-Training
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Most 3D detection algorithms are developed and validated on datasets collected during clear weather, while performance significantly deteriorates under severe weather conditions such as snowy days. To address this problem, we propose PDAST, an unsupervised pipeline for weather domain adaptation. PDAST involves point density dealing (PDD), a data augmentation method, and a density-aware pooling module (PDV), both of which are plug-and-play modules to enhance algorithmic robustness in snowy weather conditions along with the self-training [1] strategy. The data augmentation method PDD randomly samples and perturbs the ground truth point database in the point cloud. Meanwhile, the PDV module combines voxel features and density-based positional encoding features as inputs to a multi-head self-attention module, facilitating the capture of global features comprising density features. In this paper, we validate the effectiveness of PDAST on a typical voxel-based 3D detection baseline, SecondIOU [2], and conduct experiments on STF [3] datasets with clear and snowy datasets. Our approach PDAST achieves a performance enhancement of around 14.9% ~ 25.5% for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AP_{3D}$</tex> (Average Precision Of 3D Boundingboxes) and 17.5% ~ 29.3% for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AP_{AOS}$</tex> (Average Precision Of Orientation Similarity) compared to the baseline detector on clear-to-snowy conditions. Furthermore, PDAST's performance in unsupervised clear-to-snowy conditions matches or exceeds the baseline model fully supervised on snowy conditions. Our PDAST alleviates the performance degradation caused by severe weather, such as snowy days, and is of great significance for all-weather perception.

articleTitle: YOLO-SE: A Universal Real-Time Multi-Scale Object Detection Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The balance between real-time and precision is a very important consideration in object detection. Based on this objective, we present YOLO-SE, a universal real-time multi-scale object detection framework that significantly improves detection accuracy and maintains real-time performance by integrating the Standardized Enhanced Layer Aggregation Network (SE-LAN) and Frontend and Backend Feature Enhancement Blocks (FBFEB). SELAN focuses more on internal feature modules to obtain more effective multilevel features. The Frontend and Backend Feature Enhancement Blocks fully consider the enhancements that can be made to the multilevel features before and after the neck, making full use of them. The experimental results on MS COCO 2017, trained from scratch, indicate that YOLO-SE outperforms existing mainstream real-time object detection models, including the YOLO series, under the premise of similar parameters and computational complexity. YOLO-SE achieves a 4.5% and 1.5% AP increase over YOLOv8-n and YOLOv8-MS-n, respectively, and a 0.8% AP increase over RTMDet-tiny. We have provided detailed performance comparisons in the article and visualized the Grad-CAM results to provide the most intuitive results. Additionally, our SELAN and FBFEB modules can be freely replaced based on the scene, serving as plug-and-play modules for other YOLO models. The code and models of the paper are released at https://github.com/peinnn6/yolose.

articleTitle: An Efficient Highly-Secure AI-Based System for Incident Management in Critical Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The seamless operation of a critical infrastructure is achieved through a set of standard operational procedures. Leveraging new technologies to support threat management processes dramatically reduces the risk of an infrastructure outage. Moreover, private security services assess all risks to which guards are exposed and take measures to prevent dangerous situations to protect them. To handle such a problem, we present an integrated incident management system consisting of several container modules. Our loosely coupled architecture is supported by a message management framework, the main goal of which is to support the operational procedures. The proposed system, based on augmented reality and artificial intelligence, can process multiple video streams provided by closed-circuit televisions to detect possible threats related to the infrastructure. Next, it delivers the necessary information for managing an incident directly to the field and control center. The whole pipeline was employed in Preveza Marina, Greece, while tested and evaluated in real-case scenarios. Integrating such a system resulted in restructuring the standard operational procedures, permitting new security personnel management processes to safeguard health and safety during their work.

articleTitle: Elastic Weight Consolidation and Transfer Learning: A New Paradigm for Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The rampant proliferation and escalating sophistication of deepfakes underscore the critical need for effective detection mechanisms. Addressing the persistent challenge of generalization in deepfake detection, this work presents a continual learning strategy, fostering model adaptability across evolving datasets while safeguarding knowledge from prior tasks. Central to our methodology is the utilization of Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) and Layer-Wise Scaling (LWS) of learning rates. By calculating the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM), our bespoke EWC implementation adeptly counters the catastrophic forgetting dilemma. It penalizes drastic alterations in pivotal weights during incremental task training, enshrining legacy know ledge. An interesting facet of this work is the combination of EWC with transfer learning concepts. By leveraging the pre-trained Xception network, the model is imbued with a baseline of knowledge and adaptively fine-tuned for deepfake detection.

articleTitle: An Integrated CNN-RNN-SVM Framework for Classification of MRI Brain Tumor Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The early identification and categorization of brain tumor through MRI scans are pivotal for effective medical intervention. The present article encompasses a novel integrated framework that combines traditional machine learning and deep learning methods to categorize images of brain tumors. Utilizing the VGG-19 model pre-trained on ImageNet, we extract high-level features from MRI images, which are further processed by a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework to extract spatial and temporal dependencies within the data. To manage the high-dimensional feature space effectively, we employ Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction, followed by a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for the final classification task. We utilized a variety of data augmentation approach to enhance the capability of the architecture to generalize. Additionally, we fine-tuned the training parameters by employing the Adam optimizer along with early stopping and learning rate decay strategies. The model demonstrated exceptional precision, recall, and Fl-score metrics, with an accuracy of 97.86%. This study not only validates the effectiveness of integrating CNNs, RNNs, and SVMs but also opens avenues for future research in medical image analysis using hybrid deep learning frameworks. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves the accuracy of brain tumor classification compared to previous methods, offering a promising tool for aiding radiologists in the rapid and accurate diagnosis of brain tumors.

articleTitle: Positive and Unlabelled Learning with Data Approximation for Photovoltaic Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: This paper explores a Positive and Unlabeled (PU) learning framework enhanced by data approximation via Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN) for defect detection in photovoltaic cells. Employing Electroluminescence (ELPV) imaging, the proposed methodology significantly reduces the need for labeled samples, utilizing only a small subset to achieve an accuracy of 0.805 and an F1 score of 0.870. This performance is comparable to traditional supervised learning methods that use substantially more data. The results of this work validate the potential of PU learning in scenarios with limited labeled data, paving the way for future studies to optimize and expand this approach.

articleTitle: Style Transfer of Chinese Opera Character Paintings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Traditional opera character painting blends Chinese color ink painting with conventional opera, requiring both advanced opera art understanding and Chinese painting skills. However, creating these paintings demands specific artistic skills and the ability to integrate elements of opera art. Addressing these challenges is essential for the long-term development of opera character paintings and the promotion of traditional Chinese culture. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in image style transfer technology, offer new methods for generating opera character paintings. This paper uses our collected dataset of traditional opera character photographs and their paintings, employing an adversarial generative network (GAN) for implicit feature learning. Consequently, real opera character photographs are transformed into distinctive Chinese color ink paintings. To enhance the quality of the generated images, the encoding process incorporates feature mapping and attention module integration, which help reduce unimportant areas. Additionally, adaptive normalization techniques are used to improve neural network stability, accelerate convergence, and strengthen generalization capabilities. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing CNN and CycleGAN-based methods, indicates promising transfer performance and highlights the potential for the artistic creation of opera character paintings.

articleTitle: No-Reference Blurred Image Detection from Colonoscopy Videos Using Walsh-Hadamard Transform and Kolmogorov Smirnov Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Endoscopy is a widely used clinical procedure for the early detection of polyps which may develop into cancers if not treated. Colorectal cancer (CRC) being the third most diagnosed cancer in the world requires colonoscopy for diagnosis. Colonoscopy videos often contain blurry frames due to motion, out -of- focus, water jets, etc. making them prone to miss diagnosis due to information loss in the noisy frames. Image Restoration (IR) techniques such as Gaussian and diffusion-based generative denoisers have become very popular recently and have great prospects for restoring medical images. This paper proposes a simple yet effective training-free no-reference colonoscopy image blur detection technique, that can be used in future research for image denoising. This method applies artificial Gaussian blur to the input image and transforms both input and artificial blurred images from the spatial domain to the frequency domain using Walsh-Hadamard (WH) transform. Kolmogorov Smirnov test (KS-statistic) was used to calculate the difference between two distributions of frequencies assuming a blurred image will have a lower difference than a sharp image. Being training-free and using only a single frequency feature this algorithm can be implemented for any domain of images for detecting blurred images, tested on public Image Quality Assessment (IQA) datasets such as CSIQ and LIVE_II and achieved comparable results. Code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/shakhaout/colorectal-blur-detection.git

articleTitle: Automated Data Labelling for Pedestrian Crossing and Not-Crossing Actions Using 3D LiDAR and RGB Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: The existence of large-scale datasets for various autonomous driving tasks has created an increasing need for more automated annotation processes. Especially for safety critical tasks related to vehicle-pedestrian interaction, detailed and time-consuming human-made annotation is required, in order to assure accurate perception throughout any type of operating environment and for challenging conditions. In this paper, we present an automated method for the annotation of actions of humans crossing or not crossing the road. Firstly, we utilize a highly-accurate 3D multi-object tracking pipeline that combines RGB images and LiDAR data to extract the velocity and direction of movement of each pedestrian in the surrounding environment. A drivable area extraction neural network is then utilized to segment the traversable area around the vehicle. The correlation between the two above-mentioned components in the 3D space provides an accurate indication, regarding the pedestrian crossing or not-crossing the road ahead of the vehicle. Our method is validated using a custom-made multimodal dataset with an autonomous vehicle in various scenarios of a semi-structured area. The auto-generated annotations are compared directly with the human-made labels of multiple annotators and showcase the effectiveness of our method to provide an accurate indication about the human crossing the road action.

articleTitle: Testing and Evaluation of LiDAR SLAM Algorithms Based on the Combination of Virtuality and Reality Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Imaging Systems and Techniques (IST)
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), as an important means of sensing the surrounding environment, has a direct impact on the execution efficiency of autonomous grounding vehicles (UGV). At present, the most common means used to map the environment is to use hardware devices such as LiDAR, inertial measurement unit (IMU) or camera to collect data with environmental information, and then run the SLAM algorithm to construct the environment map. It is crucial by designing a system that can integrate testing and evaluation of the SLAM algorithm to promote the optimization iteration of the algorithm. In this paper, we not only collected the data from different sensors on a real UVG in the physical world test field, but also imported these data into the virtual simulation platform to construct a map of the real world test field. By maneuvering a vehicle in this virtual test field and gathering the data from the corresponding sensors installed, a typical LiDAR SLAM algorithm based on the combination of virtuality and reality was tested and evaluated as a case study.
